---
title: "Principles"
subtitle: "A hierarchical framework: one assessment logic across the data ladder, risk-equivalent advice, and the value of information"
---

The toolbox is built on a **hierarchical assessment framework** (Kell *et al.*, 2025). Stocks are assessed with whatever data exist, but the assessment logic, the biology and the definition of reference points stay the same as data are added. Advice is then **risk-equivalent**: the probability of breaching a limit is the same whichever tier a stock is assessed at, with larger precautionary buffers where information is poorer. This puts data-poor and data-moderate stocks on a common footing instead of treating them as separate, incomparable worlds.

## The data ladder

| Tier | Data | Methods in the toolbox | Status informed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Life history, exploitation history, qualitative information | [Fishery indicators](../methods/empirical/index.qmd): exploitation history, trends, dashboards, PSA for triage | Indicators and expert knowledge (indicative, not quantitative status) |
| 1 | Length compositions (by gear) | [FLicc](../methods/dynamic-pool/flicc.qmd), with [LBSPR](../methods/dynamic-pool/lbspr.qmd), [LBB](../methods/dynamic-pool/lbb.qmd) and [fishblicc](../methods/dynamic-pool/fishblicc.qmd) as special cases; [TropFishR](../methods/dynamic-pool/tropfishr.qmd) | Size structure: SPR, F/F~SPR~, selectivity |
| 2 | Catch + length | FLicc-SPM (in development) | Scale from catch, depletion from SPR, trend from length-based indicators |
| 3 | Catch + length + abundance indices | FLicc-SPM (in development); [JABBA](../methods/biomass-dynamic/jabba.qmd) and [SPiCT](../methods/biomass-dynamic/spict.qmd) with length-based F/F~MSY~ as auxiliary data | As tier 2, plus index trends |
| 4 | Catch-at-age, surveys, full integrated data | [Age-structured and integrated models](../methods/age-structured/age-structured.qmd) | All data in one likelihood |

Catch-only methods ([CMSY+](../methods/biomass-dynamic/cmsy.qmd)) sit beside the ladder rather than on it: without length data or an index, their depletion is set by priors, so they are used for triage and with explicit caution.

## One logic across tiers

- **Shared biology.** Growth, natural mortality, maturity, selectivity and steepness are defined once and used by every tier, so moving up a tier changes the information, not the assumptions.
- **Unifying model families.** On the length side, FLicc reproduces LBSPR, LBB and fishblicc as configurations of one model. FLicc-SPM extends the same model with surplus production dynamics, so that length data, catches and indices enter one likelihood. Unlike a fully structured model it does not fit the catch exactly, and it keeps uncertainty in all fits.
- **Consistent reference points.** F~SPR~ and SPR-based rules at tier 1, and F~MSY~ and B~MSY~ at tiers 2–4, come from the same per-recruit model.

## Value of information

Because the tiers share one model and one set of assumptions, the contribution of each data source can be measured directly: run the same stock at each tier and compare how well status and advice recover the truth.

- **Simulated twins:** operating models with known truth (for example the FLicc simulator, the cpueTargeting and mmsyFM operating models) generate catches, indices and length compositions for the same stock.
- **Metrics by tier:** bias and precision of B/B~MSY~ and F/F~MSY~, probability of misclassifying status, and the buffer needed for risk-equivalent advice, by exploitation phase (fishing down, rebuilding).
- **Real data:** the same comparisons on well-studied stocks (for example ICES case studies) where a data-rich assessment serves as a benchmark.

The answer guides two decisions: which method a stock's data support now, and which data collection would improve advice most.

## One standard of good practice

Risk equivalence only holds if every assessment that informs advice, at every tier, has passed the same standard of scrutiny. The toolbox adopts the four objective properties of a plausible model (Carvalho *et al.*, 2021): **convergence**, **fit to the data**, **model consistency** and **prediction skill**, with **plausibility** (consistency with the biology and the exploitation history) as the overarching check. No single diagnostic is used in isolation to accept or reject a model. For surplus production models these are made operational in the good practice guidelines of Kokkalis *et al.* (2024); the [model acceptance checklist](../guidance/diagnostics.qmd#model-acceptance-checklist) applies them across the toolbox.

## How the toolbox puts this into practice

| Principle | Where in the toolbox |
|---|---|
| Know your data first | [Data preparation workflow](../data-tools/data-preparation.qmd) |
| Match the method to the tier | [Method selector](../select/index.qmd), [hierarchy](hierarchy.qmd) |
| Use methods within their assumptions | Misuse prevention on every page; [misuse rules](../guidance/misuse.qmd) |
